prompt:
You watch a short video made ONLY of these clips, played back to back with NO narration between them.
Each clip is a person's own words from a show; the shows were not in one conversation. The first clip (label "hook")
opens the video.

CLIP label="hook" (on screen: Simply Bitcoin): "A CEO makes a personal mistake in shareholders pay. A government mismanages its currencies. and its savers pay. Bitcoin's rules aren't kept by a single executive or a single central bank. They're enforced by thousands of independent computers running the same code. No CEO, no compromise, no committee to debate."
CLIP label="clip_01" (on screen: Scott Melker): "My biggest fear is that I go to the bank and I punch you my code and the money's not there because the bank owns the money and they could just take it from me. And that's why we Bitcoin."
CLIP label="clip_02" (on screen: Stephan Livera): "In a way, I think of Bitcoin being like this global productivity index, similar to the S &P 500 is to individual stocks."
CLIP label="clip_03" (on screen: Digital Asset News): "You can, I mean, for Pete's sakes, Jack Dorsey on Block was giving you money about a year ago. And all he had to do was just buy stuff with Bitcoin. And very few people did it. And he turned on this, this, what was it called? The Bitcoin spigot."

1) Played back to back with no narration, is there a through-line a viewer can state? State it in ONE sentence, or
   "none" if there is none.
2) THE HOOK is judged on its own job, NOT on the through-line. Rate each of its three parts 1-5 separately:
   "scroll": do its first 2-3 seconds stop a viewer from scrolling past? (5 = certainly, 1 = not at all)
   "alone": does it stand alone, so that a viewer needs nothing said before it? (5 = fully, 1 = not at all)
   "setup": does it set up what follows, so that a viewer who hears it wants the next clip? (5 = certainly, 1 = not
   at all)
3) For each clip AFTER the hook, rate 1-5 how much it advances that through-line (5 = essential, 1 = off topic).
4) For each JOIN between two consecutive clips: could a viewer follow the jump with no narration, i.e. is the next
   clip's subject or referent clear coming from the previous clip's ending? Answer true or false, and why in a few
   words.
Return ONLY this JSON object: {"through_line": "...", "hook": {"scroll": 1, "alone": 1, "setup": 1},
"clips": {"clip_01": 1, "clip_02": 1, "clip_03": 1}, "joins": {"hook -> clip_01": {"followable": true, "why": "..."}, "clip_01 -> clip_02": {"followable": true, "why": "..."}, "clip_02 -> clip_03": {"followable": true, "why": "..."}}}
text: {"through_line": "Bitcoin as a decentralized alternative to centralized finance, moving from its structural advantages to its macro significance to its real-world adoption.", "hook": {"scroll": 3, "alone": 5, "setup": 3}, "clips": {"clip_01": 4, "clip_02": 3, "clip_03": 3}, "joins": {"hook -> clip_01": {"followable": true, "why": "Hook ends on 'no CEO, no central bank'; clip_01 gives a personal fear of the bank, same centralized-institution subject."}, "clip_01 -> clip_02": {"followable": true, "why": "Clip_01 ends 'that's why we Bitcoin'; clip_02 pivots to a new framing of what Bitcoin is, subject carries over."}, "clip_02 -> clip_03": {"followable": false, "why": "S&P 500 macro-index framing does not logically lead to a Dorsey spigot adoption anecdote; referent shifts abruptly."}}}
